candidates.background: Chilmeran is the Green Party nominee in the three-way District 61 race. According to the Branch voter guide, she grew up in McKinney, graduated from Austin College in Sherman, works as a Realtor and previously worked as a paralegal. No campaign platform from her was found online.

notes.text: Did not respond to the 2026 ATPE candidate survey or the iVoterGuide questionnaire, according to those organizations.
The Branch voter guide reported that as of September 11, 2026 she had no campaign website or issue information online.

candidates.research_gaps: No campaign platform, issue positions or questionnaire answers were found; only basic biographical details from a voter guide.

promises.text: Says she supports raising the basic allotment and using part of the state budget surplus and Rainy Day Fund to stabilize school funding, with flexible dollars for districts.
Says she supports a state-funded, across-the-board pay raise for all school employees, tied to inflation and regional cost of living.
Says she supports a larger state contribution to TRS-ActiveCare and TRS-Care and keeping TRS a defined-benefit pension.

notes.text: Her campaign site also lists support from Public Schools First McKinney, Teachers Unify Action, Vote Save America, Blue Horizon Texas PAC, McKinney ISD trustee Harvey Oaxaca and state Reps. Gene Wu and Christina Morales.

issue_notes.summary: Opposes using a single testing model to set teacher pay or A-F school ratings and favors multiple measures such as student growth and graduation outcomes.

q_deportation.summary: Says local law enforcement should focus on community safety rather than serving as an extension of federal immigration politics, and opposes using border policy as an excuse for unconstitutional overreach.

q_preemption.summary: Says the state should set broad standards without micromanaging, and that local districts should keep authority over curriculum and that local control should stay local instead of being handed off to Austin.

sources.title: Brittany Black: responses to the 2026 ATPE candidate survey

promises.text: Says her first legislative priority is to immediately end education savings accounts and school vouchers.
Says she would raise the basic allotment by at least $1,000 per student and set a minimum teacher salary of at least $65,000, paid for with the state surplus.
Says she supports a state-funded, across-the-board pay raise for all educators and wants the state to match district contributions to TRS.

notes.text: Her campaign lists endorsements from Moms Demand Action (Gun Sense Candidate), McKinney Area Democrats, Mothers Against Greg Abbott, Save Our Public Schools, Collin County Democrats with Disabilities, Mental Health Now and Blue Horizon.

issue_notes.summary: Opposes the new through-year testing model under HB 8 and says test results should never be the sole factor in A-F ratings or used to penalize teachers financially.
Her campaign blog criticizes how the state education savings account program is run, including the vendor contract and the share of applicants already paying for private school.

q_gun_laws.summary: Told ATPE that improving school safety in the long term would require fundamental reforms to gun laws, and is designated a Gun Sense Candidate by Moms Demand Action.

promises.text: Says he will support legislation to attract more insurers to Texas, incentives for disaster-resistant home upgrades and improvements to the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association to lower insurance costs.
Says he will work to fund school resource officers, threat detection technology and more school counselors.
Says he will push for transparency in insurance billing and protection from surprise medical bills.

notes.text: His campaign lists endorsements from Moms Demand Action (Gun Sense Candidate), Collin County Stonewall Democrats, Asian American Democrats of Texas, Plano Area Democrats, Frisco Democratic Club, Mental Health Now, The Hindu American PAC and the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, among others.

issue_notes.summary: Proposes more insurer competition, state-backed incentives for storm-resistant homes, rate transparency and stronger state risk pools to lower home and auto insurance costs.
Supports investment in local law enforcement with accountability, community-based crime prevention, mental health and drug treatment programs, and more support for crime victims.

q_gun_laws.summary: Designated a Gun Sense Candidate by Moms Demand Action, a group that backs background checks and red flag laws; no direct statement on gun laws was found.

q_medicaid.summary: His campaign site supports exploring a state-managed Medicaid expansion with accountability measures and cost caps (replaces a stronger rating based on a third-party summary, since his own wording is conditional).

q_abortion.summary: Says Texans deserve a choice and that health care decisions should be made between a patient and a doctor without government interference (strengthened from his campaign site's own wording).

record.text: Voted for H.J.Res. 35 in February 2025, which repealed the EPA rule implementing the methane Waste Emissions Charge for oil and gas operations; it passed 220 to 206.
Voted against the SAFE Banking Act in 2021 and against the MORE Act and the Medical Marijuana Research Act in 2022.
Voted for the District of Columbia Federal Immigration Compliance Act and the Save SBA from Sanctuary Cities Act in June 2025, and the Deporting Fraudsters Act in March 2026.
Voted against H.R. 1689 in April 2026, which would require designating Haiti for temporary protected status; it passed 224 to 204.
Voted for the Protecting American Energy Production Act (H.R. 26) in February 2025, which bars a presidential moratorium on hydraulic fracturing.

q_oilgas_rules.summary: Voted in 2025 to repeal the EPA rule implementing the methane emissions charge on oil and gas operations.

q_cannabis.summary: Voted against the MORE Act to remove marijuana from federal controlled substances, the SAFE Banking Act and the Medical Marijuana Research Act.

q_deportation.summary: Voted for bills requiring local cooperation with ICE and penalizing sanctuary jurisdictions, and said the 2025 reconciliation law's ICE funding helps deport criminal illegal aliens.

q_legal_status.summary: Has said allowing mass unlawful migration and letting people cut the line is patently unfair, and voted against a 2026 bill to grant Haiti temporary protected status.

q_fossil_priority.summary: Campaigns on expanding energy production and voted for a 2025 bill barring a presidential moratorium on hydraulic fracturing.

record.text: Voted for SB 3 (2023, fourth called session), appropriating funds for border barrier construction and border security operations; it passed the Senate 18 to 10.
Voted for SB 4 (2023, fourth called session), creating state offenses for illegal entry and authorizing removal orders; it passed the Senate 17 to 11.

Voted for SB 421 (2019), relating to acquisition of real property by entities with eminent domain authority, which passed 28 to 3, and SB 726 (2021), on landowners' right to repurchase condemned property, which passed 27 to 4.

q_border_state.summary: Voted for 2023 state funding for border barrier construction and border security operations (SB 3).

q_deportation.summary: Voted for the 2023 state illegal entry and removal law (SB 4) and the 2025 sheriff ICE agreement law (SB 8), and says state officials should ban sanctuary cities.

q_eminent_domain.summary: Voted for 2019 and 2021 Senate bills on eminent domain acquisitions and landowners' right to repurchase condemned property.

q_ethics.summary: His campaign calls for much higher standards in state government ethics and transparency; no statement on contribution limits was found.
